review:
After several days of heavy playing and finally finishing the whole story, I'm bringing myself back here to write my very first game review. I started playing the AC series from AC2 which is an epic game. Besides the rises and falls of public opinion toward this brand name, I've always liked the past AC games (yes, even the Unity which everybody shitted on). Game makers are trying very hard to continue the story, and I truly appreciate their efforts. 

Some of the best things about ACO that I really like:

1. Architecture. This is the best thing about AC games. For me, it's since I first "ran" across Venice Rooftops. I could just sit at the top of the Pyramid of Giza and stare at this fabulous world all day long. 

2. Combat. Alright, I have complex feelings about this one. Combat is really hard compared to previous AC games, where you could basically just do counters and take down as many guards as there possibly are. Being surrounded would be a nightmare in ACO when you're not well-equipped enough. Luckily boss battles are not hell because you mostly only need to deal with one, and then you can truly analyze their attacking patterns and fight accordingly. BTW, I started using long-ranged predator bows to assassinate most of the normal guards. Super fun controlling the arrow in air and headshotting around the corner, and helps you avoid so much conflict.

3. Resource gathering. I think this is where the game makers really gave some thoughts. You never have excess money or resources, but you never lack a whole lot of them either. You won't have to spend a lot of time to gather some key resources for one or two important upgrade that might get you through one major quest. Super equipments are not hard to get either, Reda the You Also Grow Too Fast kid sells this chest in which legendary ranked stuff are not scarce. All these make the balance just about right between going through the main story and doing random training and gathering to leveling up. 

4. Photo mode. Haha this one is just SUPER! This could keep some people playing for a long while. Now those beautiful sceneries would never be wasted again. And you have a bunch of options to play with to make your favorite photo. Also, you can see other amazing photos taken by other players as well in the map tab. Also, those photos might contain information about the location as well, sometimes useful.

5. Senu. She is the Origin of the Eagle Vision and she is the BEST so far. This system helps you locate objects, treasures, animals, enermies and even entrances, but you do have to manually scan the map to pin them all. Again, I think it's just about right in terms of balance.


That being said, some other not too positive thougts too.
6. Level system. This kind of started since Syndicate where the ability points system is introduced. But... you have to upgrade hidden blade damage, or otherwise you can't even do half hp damage to a high level captain or commander when "assassinating" from behind? That just feels weird. Thankfully leveling up and collecting material to upgrade, say your hidden blade (at least to a "usable" degree for your current mission) would not be too much of a hassle, otherwise this system would be really annoying.

7. Story. 
7.1 I really liked Bayek's story, but I don't see why... alright I'm not turning myself into a spoiler. Anyways, I see others complaining that every AC game gives a new definition of the Creed, but I kinda disagree with that. Nobody said that game makers advocated what they where conveying through the characters. We see that in AC3 where the game itself spoke for Haythem's Templar logic and criticized Conner's brute work to some extent. The debate between ideologies never stopped, and as a game series, I think AC is still handling itself okay in this context. I believe that if you have played AC3 before, you would probably feel as I do that Bayek is not much better than Conner when Conner started his journey. But the idea Bayek and Aya put forward toward the end of ACO did make sense and was a good explanation for the Origin of the brotherhood. But besides from that, I still find the story lacking the impact I had when playing AC2, Revelations, Black Flag or Rogue. 
7.2 In addition, the modern timeline didn't progress much either... I'm really not interested in picking up all the novels and stuff, and I know none of the characters in ACO except for William Miles (whom I only know as much as that he is Desmond's father). I'll just wait for the next AC game and see if the modern timeline could make any sense. I hope it does. Well, you could actually find clues in ACO but... Again, I'm not gonna be a spoiler.

8. Music. It's nowhere near bad. Actually I think it's good and immersive. But Venice Rooftops and Ezio's Family just couldn't be beaten. 

To the end of this pile of rubbish I just talked, I like this game very much. But I guess that nobody actually cares, lol. Those who are not interested will probably still not buy this game after reading all those positive reviews, and those who are interested already bought and shot the sh*t out of Anubis haha. Good luck hunting hippos everybody!

Whether or not you’ll enjoy this game largely depends on what you value as a player. If you’re looking for deep and well-thought-out gameplay, you’ll probably be disappointed, unless you’re a big fan of Ubisoft’s typical formula. However, if you love immersing yourself in an atmospheric world with engaging stories, this game could be a solid choice.

One major strength of the gameplay is the variety of weapon types, each supporting different playstyles. You also have a lot of freedom in how you approach missions, which is refreshing. However, the mechanics as a whole are rather shallow and lack depth. Players who prioritize intricate gameplay and well-designed enemies might find it lacking, especially when it comes to the few boss fights, which are neither particularly challenging nor creative. As such, the game is more tailored to casual players. Even though I played it on "Hard," I never felt it offered any real challenge.

Where the game truly shines is in its worldbuilding and the stories it tells. The world feels authentic and alive, making it a joy to explore and learn about the lives of its inhabitants. The only real drawback is the connection to the "Assassin’s Creed" franchise, which feels misplaced and out of place. It frequently pulls you out of the otherwise captivating world. A completely new IP would have been a far better approach than trying to reboot the "Assassin’s Creed" series in this way.

This is arguably one of the best games set in an ancient world, showcasing just how much potential this kind of setting holds. Exploring the world feels refreshing and captivating, adding a unique charm to the experience.

Another major positive is that Ubisoft’s typical open-world formula is entirely optional here. You’re not forced to grind through it. While it provides resources and new weapons, you can safely ignore it if you wish. The game gives you enough to progress without needing to "check off" everything. You can simply do what interests you and leave the rest behind.

Overall, this game is aimed at players looking for a relaxed experience with engaging stories, rather than hardcore gamers seeking challenges and complex gameplay. I bought the game at a steep discount and found it quite entertaining for the price. However, I played it more casually, as the gameplay was too simplistic to keep me engaged for long sessions. My expectations were realistic, though, and I got exactly what I hoped for, making the experience worthwhile.

[h1]My overall thoughts[/h1]
Assassin’s Creed Origins is an attempt to bring in new ideas by taking cues from the recent RPGs while trying to retain the soul of the series. To that attempt, I say it has succeeded. The vast expanse of Egypt is breathtaking. The new style of combat is amazing and the narrative has you dig deep into the origins of the Creed, the handbook of the world’s most spiritual killers. I’ve been always been an Assassin’s creed apologist and even when playing unity and syndicate, I found many redeemable qualities.

However, the franchise’s lethargy soon rubbed off on me I was finally going to give up. I mean come on, I liked Unity but Syndicate came off nothing more than an attempt to rectify Unity’s mistake. It made me want to assassinate the franchise. But that all changed with AC Origins, a game that I couldn’t stop playing and finally made me fall in love with the Franchise again.  

[h1]Plot[/h1]

You follow Bayek of Siwa, an Egyptian badass and the last Medjay of Egypt. He is on the quest to avenge the death (I know) of his young son by the hands of “masked ones” – an order of proto templars who you chase around all through Egypt. Along the way, you will meet characters such as the brotherly Phanos, the cowardly Ptolemy, the seductress Cleopatra and the conniving Julius Ceasar. The story is weaved in long and drawn-out quests whose pay off makes it almost worth it. 

As you can guess, I like the story. While it’s the same my-family-got-murdered-and-I-gotta-murder-the-murderer-too feel of the old games, I like the fact that here, the main character is a father. You see several layers of Bayek. He comes off as kind and playful to help-seekers and rage-filled god of death to the killers. The storytelling is fairly linear but that grips you from start to finish, with you hoping that in the end, Bayek finds some happiness. 

[h1]Presentation[/h1]
The vast expanse of Egypt is breath-taking. From the populated cities to depilated caves, from the mysterious pyramids to the historic Alexandria, every inch of recreated Egypt oozes care and detail. It’s further complemented by the game excellent lighting system, where you can feel the dizzying warmth of the sun as you run or cart over the land of this new playground. The water physics were the best of 2017 and 18, and even 20. 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

[b]Combat[/b] 

Combat has been completely overhauled in this game. The counter kill manoeuvres of the previous titles has been replaced by a hitbox mechanic. The combat is complemented by different classes of weapons including Staves, spears, regular sword, khopesh, dual daggers, maces and heavy swords. Each weapon has a unique weight behind it and provides a different way of playstyle. 

Another major change in combat is the addition of ranged combat. You now have a bow and not just of a single kind. There is a multi-arrow-spitting warrior bow, a precise-hitting hunter bow, a scope-wielding predator bow and a fast and magnificent light bow. While predator and hunter bows are helpful in stealth, warrior and light bows scream style in combat sections.
The game allows you to equip to melee and two range weapons. Strategize, choose and switch them as per your playstyle anytime as you face challenges from enemies, both man and beasts. 

[b]Stealth[/b]

Continuing the “innovation” of a dedicated crouch button in Unity, AC origins gives you the ability to crouch behind your enemy as you stab him with your pre-assassin hidden blade. The addition of many ranged weapon options has you meticulously pick off your enemies from a distance. Stealth is satisfying – giving you a rising feeling as you clear out a camp of Roman soldiers without even a single soul screaming. 

[b]Exploration[/b]

Egypt is vast, and I mean ridiculously vast. You can travel across horseback, camelback or chariot on the road for a faster traversal. On the river, you have boats. The series’ staple parkour mechanics are back. However, they don’t give the same feeling as in the previous games. One can say the parkour has been put on the back burner to make room new ways to explore the desert wonder. And boy there is a lot to explore. There are caves, bandit camps, underwater treasure bellies and more. 

None of the exploration options is without rewards. Other than being a completionist’s wet dream of checklist gaming, it also provides you with ample of side quests. There are over 100 side quests and all of them have something to add to either the character or the narrative of the game. 

[b]RPG elements[/b]

In the series’ first, traditional RPG elements are weaved into the game with three classes of abilities to develop: Warrior, Hunter and seeker. As you complete quests and explore the world, you gain experience points that you can to put in either one or all of those classes. The quality of abilities you get range from effective to mediocre to obtuse. Although the addition is appreciated, you can see that this is just Ubi’s attempt to see how the new elements work out. 

[b]Online Elements[/b]

AC Origins is one of the victims of mobile-gaming models that have slithered their ways in Single Player Games. There are events and daily missions, giving you a chance to take a bite of that legendary loot you've been eyeing for so long. Daily missions give you two types of quests: fetch and assassinations. However, the events contain climatic and challenging boss battles that are rewarding quite on their own. 

However, the rate of loot drops is painfully low, forcing a grind that while enjoyable, is still a grind. And it doesn't help that the in-your-face microtransaction model that Ubi has been peddling to compensate for the rarity of loot drops is quite pathetic. That being said, it won't affect your gameplay experience, and you, like me can get quite a lot of loot without spending one penny. Just be ready to invest a lot of time in the desert. 

[h1]How well it plays?[/h1]

The game is demanding. While I wasn’t expecting for a potato to run it, I was hoping for some levity for mid-level machines. While desert regions can help you maintain constant 60, prepare to drop 10 29 in populated cities. 

[h1]Is it worth it?[/h1]

Assassin’s Creed Origins is borne out of the passion of its developers. The narrative main quests, the engaging side quests, the amazing gameplay can entertain you for hours. However, make sure that your machine has enough juice to experience it all. You can get lost in its details and even after 150 hours of gameplay, I’ve yet to see everything the game has to offer. However, the microtransactions don’t bode well for the direction the series is taking.

[b]On that note, I give this game an 8 out of 10.[/b]

I am an adventure gamer, at heart, and have only recently tested the waters of action/adventures. After completing Horizon Zero Dawn and the Tomb Raider games, I was hooked. Since I generally suck at combat (although I am improving), I began playing Assassin's Creed Origins on 'Easy' and fell in love with the game. 120+ hours later I have opened up the entire map, completed every side-quest I could find, and successfully achieved the objectives at all locations that are visible to this point. My character is at level 40 and I have some pretty awesome armor, weapons, and an eagle as a traveling companion. 

You play as Bayek of Siwa - A Medjay  and assassin operating in Egypt during the time of Cleopatra and Ptolemy. While many of the pyramids and monuments are past their prime, the cities are colorful and alive. You get a glimpse of what it might have been like to live during this era. The geography is vast... you can walk city streets, ride a camel across endless sand dunes, sail a boat down the Nile, gallop a horse along winding roads, or deep dive in the Mediterranean.  You encounter bandits, wild beasts, ship wrecks, ruins, ancient machinery and tombs. All in all, it is an amazingly open world with beautiful vistas and more content than one can imagine. 

Although the primary plot is driven by a series of assassinations, the Medjay are protectors and Bayek is a champion for the downtrodden. I found it satisfying to play a good guy and direct the violence towards those in power who were dangerous and corrupt. There is some political intrigue but this is not the main theme.

For an adventurer, the combat is straight forward and simple to master. The statistics on weapons and armor do not require a degree in mathematics, and skills acquired are not a burden to activate. You have the option of approaching with stealth to take enemies by surprise or you can go in with swords and spears blazing.  

There is an abundance of trinkets to loot, resources to find/steal, riddles to solve, and treasure to plunder. You can trade with local merchants, using drachmas as the coin of the realm.

Plan to do A LOT of traveling if you are a player who enjoys side quests and errands. For me, this was enjoyable and the fast-travel feature shortened many of my treks across different regions. 

My only complaint is that there is a naval combat sequence near the end that has me absolutely stuck. Until I sink the last enemy ship, I cannot continue with the game. Even in 'easy' mode, this exercise is quite tough for me and there is no way around it. If at first you don't succeed, try (and try and try and try) again...

I highly recommend this game to adventurers who seek a unique experience with combat, exploration, a likable character, and an interesting story.

[code]Assassin’s Creed Origins proved to be a much needed & mostly fun overhaul for the long-running franchise but a new direction also introduces new problems - and some surprising downgrades when compared to its predecessors[/code]

After 2015’s [i]Assassin’s Creed Syndicate[/i], it almost seemed like the franchise was nearing it’s creative end. The “classic [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] formula” had been repeated for far too long at this point, with recurring criticisms that [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/dreamylotus/recommended/368500/]didn’t only apply to one, but many of the games[/url]. Many grew tired of playing the “same game” over & over and this (or rather the resulting poor sales) didn’t go unnoticed by publisher Ubisoft as well. The franchise went on a short creative break (apart from the release of the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/dreamylotus/recommended/359600/]awful Chronicles 2.5D spinoff trilogy[/url]) and it was two years later, in 2017, that [i]Assassin’s Creed Origins[/i] was released: An open-world action-RPG with completely overhauled gameplay systems and a story set in ancient Egypt, detailing the founding of the brotherhood & thus happening way before the previous [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] games.

Along with a new present day story (an incredibly short one, totaling ~30min in length), this does make [i]Origins[/i] a great pick for newcomers to the franchise: It might not be a narrative reboot but considering it’s aforementioned time & setting, it can be treated as a prequel to the other [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] games with no additional lore knowledge required. That said, the beginning of [i]Origins[/i] is one of the weaker parts of the game, throwing you right into the middle of things and only starting to properly explain characters and their motivations afterwards.

[i]Origins[/i] features a more character-centric story this time around, as the classic [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] factions (brotherhood/templars) naturally haven’t been around yet. It’s an intriguing tale, making full use of the unique setting and offering some “so that’s why”-moments for fans of the franchise along the usual twists, turns and betrayals. It’s great at guiding you through the world and offers some nice setpieces this time around, however, it’s also held back by some lacking characterizations, resulting in one-dimensional villains, some awkwardly stiff cutscenes and – most egregiously – pacing issues.

These pacing issues mainly stem from the [i]Origins[/i] gameplay overhaul  and the new RPG-elements: almost everything in the game, be it the player, locations, enemies or quests, is attributed with a level now. If an enemy is four levels higher than the player’s level, they’re basically impossible to beat, since you’re barely going scratch them thanks to damage scaling while they’re going to kill you in ~2 hits. You might be able to kill a hyena in the starting region with no trouble at all, for example, but if you meet another hyena ~50m away in a high-level region, it might take you down in one hit. As such, you have no choice but to meet the level requirements for the main story missions – but if you’re just sticking with only doing story content, you’ll quickly become underleveled as they don’t provide sufficient XP rewards. No, even if you’re the type of player who only goes for story quests, [i]Origins[/i] forces you to engage with side content to meet the level requirements.

Notably, if you own the [i]Curse of the Pharaos[/i] DLC, you’ll have access to a level booster, which allows you to skip the side content grind. But even if there’s an (optional) option to scale enemies to your level in order to keep the game from being a cakewalk, using the level booster also upgrades your entire weaponry and grants you all of the crafting upgrades (e.g. more health, higher damage, etc.), which has the unfortunate side effect of nearly all quests/activities now providing rewards that you can’t really use anymore – so be careful if you’re thinking about level-boosting.

In case you rather want to do side content instead, the vast Egypt of [i]Origins[/i] does not only offer a large variety of biomes - lots of deserts, mountains, swamps, farmlands and Egytpian/Roman/Greek cities - but also many different side activities from quests, to explorable tombs or challenges like arena fights or horse racing. Some surprisingly big patches of the map might be disappointingly life- and content-less, but the vast majority of it is filled to the brim with these optional activities to participate in, which are either about exploring, fighting enemies or solving smaller puzzles/riddles. Finishing all of them which should easily grant you 80+h of playtime, however. you’ll also realize that many side activities are basically the same, just placed in different locations (e.g. enemy camps always asking you to kill a certain guard and collect a certain amount of treasure). The side quests, on the other hand, usually allow you to learn more about the area you’re currently exploring.

Apart from the side content feeding into new level, loot & upgrade systems, which also come with a skill tree to unlock new abilities, combat and movement have been completely reworked in [i]Origins[/i]. Assassinations are only insta-kills if the enemies are about (or lower than) your level now, which unfortunately makes them less useful – especially since the game also forces you to participate in direct boss fights, which won’t even allow for stealth approaches. Similarly, the parkour system has been significantly scaled back compared to [i]Unity[/i] or [i]Syndicate[/i] , offering fewer player control and options for free-running.

[i]Origins[/i] features a typical action-RPG lock-on combat system now: various weapon types for close and ranged combat, normal and (chargeable) heavy attacks, shielding, dodging, parrying and “special attacks” once a certain gauge has been filled by performing combos. It works just as you probably imagine it does, although the “lock-on” function can’t really handle multiple enemies. Also, while some fights in [i]Origins[/i] can prove challenging, the game cares more about your level than your actual combat performance – as mentioned earlier, even if you’re well-versed in the combat system, high-level enemies will still be impossible to beat thanks to the damage scaling.

Overall, however, as long as you’re engaging with the huge amount of side content often enough and stay in the level-appropriate regions/quests, [i]Origins[/i] should prove to be an enjoyable experience as long as you’re into the gameplay loop of exploring, finishing activities, getting rewarded and continuing the journey. Fans of the franchise might be disappointed that assassinations and parkour are less important than levels and loot now but the “classic” mechanics still have their place in the game, albeit less prominently. Also, while the present-day story might be disappointingly shallow, the nods to later [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] entries should appeal to longtime-fans as well. Players that play games primarily for an uninterrupted story experience or simply dislike grinding (similar) side-content might lose their patience with [i]Origins[/i], however.

Considering the success of [i]Origins[/i], it’s fair to say that the new action-RPG direction of the franchise was the right choice for many players . aIthough Ubisoft still doesn't manage to deliver a game experience without technical problems. In my case, these included the game refusing to run on a previously selected monitor, crashes, savegames vanishing (back them up!) and even a bug where [i]Origins[/i] basically starts running & using resources as soon as you turn on your PC, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/582160/discussions/1/3409804429007189920/]entirely by itself[/url]. It's simply disappointing that Ubisoft didn't manage to fix these issues after all these years, so be warned - the game itself is worth it but only if it works.

[quote][b]OVERVIEW[/b] ↴[/quote]
Assassin's Creed Origins is an amazing action-adventure stealth game experience for a single player set in Ancient Egypt near the end of the Ptolemaic period (49–44 BC), and recounts the secret but fictional history of once a proud kingdom, now a divided region. We take on a role of a Medjay named Bayek of Siwa, who works to protect the people of the Ptolemaic Kingdom during a time of widespread upheaval between Ptolemy XIII, Cleopatra and Julius Caesar fighting for control... and explore the origins of the centuries long conflict between the Hidden Ones (the Brotherhood of Assassins), and The Order of the Ancients (the Templar Order) which was responsible for the death of Bayek's son, Khemu, that leads our main protagonist into exile to seek vengeance.

[quote][b]GRAPHICS AND AUDIO[/b] ↴[/quote]
I feel like Origins can easily join ranks amongst those games with an outstanding qualities and nearly perfect beautiful design. The vast expanse of the region we get to play in is breath-taking and definitely one of the most amazing environments I've seen. I'm not kidding when I say that everywhere you look you can see the jawdropping details of graphics and physics that are making this game almost ageless. And it's even futher complemented by things like an authentic feeling of this very fascinating time period of civil war the game is set but also an excellent lighting system, which actually makes you feel the dizzying heat of the sun as you explore each district with it's own unique and mysterious sights from the populated cities to hidden cavern passages to even underwater plains full of interesting treasures. And all of this is accompanied by a great score (could listen to the main theme for the rest of my life) and nicely done sound design that works well with the visuals of the game to immerse you into an amazing and intriguing atmosphere of Ancient Egypt. (Ps. Photo mode for the win!)

[quote][b]GAMEPLAY[/b] ↴[/quote]
Compared to the previous games combat in AC Origins has been completley revamped. While the old system of an enemies was heavily based on them attacking you one at a time which made you capable of simply countering all their moves in a never-ending cycle, the new one is more of an RPG style that is significantly harder but also considerably more satisfying. One-on-one attacks are no longer applied but instead a variety of enemies with different attacks, from melee to long-ranged one, can start a fight with you more than two or even three at a time from every possible angle. Before you where getting an easy wins with pressing the counter symbol at a right time, however now to win combat scenarios it's essential for you to level up and have a good gear/weapons equipped (which we can have our pick of since the game offers us different classes of weapons and each one has its unique weight/stats that can provide usvwith a bit of a different way of playstyle). This gives the combat attacks quite the variety as the enemies will definitely not wait in line for their chance to take a hit at you anymore. I think this a great change in the system since now you can feel more like an assassin workin in the shadows to outsmart his foes and this is where we're getting a pretty huge emphasis on stealth and stategic thinking... simply analyzing the patterns, planing your attacks and all that or even finding a quick route of escape since it's no longer so easy to rush in to a fort, due to it being harder than it was before. And let me tell you that clearing out a whole camp of soldiers without even a single soul screaming out for alarm - satisfying as hell. I mean, sure, you can still try charging in there without planing anything out but don't be surprised if you fail miserably at killing your target and you end up as an avenge quest for other players to find. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

[quote][b]STORY[/b] ↴[/quote]
When we start the game, the Assassin order does not even exist. Instead we learn a story of a Medjay, Bayek of Siwa at a time where the words "I am a Medjay. I am a feather in the eagle's wing... a living dagger, plunged from the sky into the heart of chaos. I am a truth unknown... a scabbard unfilled... a son of the Nile... and a defender of the people. You cannot kill me, for I walk among the dead. Come forth by day, and I will guide you home." are getting a new meaning after he suffers a great lost at the hands of a mysterious figures standing behind the Order of the Ancients which drastically changes his point of view and making him become Medjay to no pharaoh, a hidden one, a protector not only for the people of his region but the whole realm. And this where our journey begins...

[quote][b]PERFORMANCE, BUGS AND GLITCHES[/b] ↴[/quote]
Ehh... there were a some lil' bugs and glitches but mostly the hilarious kind of ones. For example, the ship flying in the sky and then doing it's own re-edition of sinking Titanic, and like c'mon, that flying horse/camel doing cartwheel, anyone? I bet there are few more out there but I didn't encounter anything game-breaking.

[quote][b]CONCLUSION[/b] ↴[/quote]
Origins left me deeply impressed not only with it's unique and breathtaking landscape that stretched for what felt like an eternity but also with the attention to detail for the main story set in Ancient Egypt as well as all the small but gripping story lines that painted an interesting picture for the player. It actually made me feel like every single minute was worth playing and this game without a doubt surpassed my expectations. I cannot find a single thing (except being forced to play as Aya) that I didn't enjoy in this insane world that's a completionist’s wet dream. Seriously, it was a joy to get lost in exploring. That's why I think it's a must have for adventure enthusiasts like me and all those who complain about this game being a walking simulator don't have a real appreciation for a masterpiece this game truly is. For me this entry in Assassin's Creed series is one of the best in the franchise as a whole and it's gonna be very hard to change my mind about that. My bff already tried, didn't worked at all.

[h1][b]Assassin’s Creed Origins[/b][/h1]
[i]Assassin's Creed Origins[/i] is a open world, action, stealth, rpg and a game which changed Assassin's Creed forever.

Origins is the first of its type in this franchise and people are not often too happy about changes. Since I’m a big fan of the older Assassin’s Creed games I was a bit hesitate at first but after playing it for a bit I started to enjoy the new type of gameplay and its features.

Is Origins a bad game? Simply said: No it really isnt but its something different from what we have seen from this franchise and it made a lot of good changes in my opinion. If you like RPGs, stealth games and fights with quite a bit of action you might also like Assassin’s Creed Origins since this game is a mix out of all of those genres. 

[b]Story[/b]

The player is controlling Bayek of Siwa who is looking for the people that were responsible for his sons death. His wife Aya of Alexandria is joining Bayek in his path of vengeance. Throughout the story the plot thickens and the player will encounter famous characters like Cleopatra VII and Julius Caesar.

The Story is very Assassin’s Creed like with the usual fair share of actual historical events and made up things that the player discovers throughout the playthrough. The whole events of Origins are set in the ancient egypt which is quite a cool setting for me personally – if you like the setting you should give it a try.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1981880092
[b]Personal note[/b]

When I started playing this game I was quite hesitate as I mentioned earlier. I couldnt imagine how an Assassin’s Creed game could become an RPG. After playing it for maybe 6 hours I started to like the changes and the new possibilities that Origins implemented. 

I was a bit disappointed that the focus of Origins wasnt mainly on the stealth gameplay, which older games, in this franchise were so focused on. After a while I learned to like that though, since sometimes you dont feel like sneaking through a whole garrison when you simply can take a fight.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2061910510
I quickly started to do some side quests instead of following the main quest which kind of boosted me because I was leveling quite fast, which gave me an advantage when I came back to do the main story line. I really fell in love with being able to do whatever I liked to do – when I felt like doing some exploring while following some side quest plots, I was able to do so and it felt so fresh with the RPG elements in the game.

[b]Rating[/b]
[list][b]Pros[/b]
[*]The fighting feels pretty good
[*]The RPG elements are well executed
[*]Eagle Vision ability is pretty cool
[*]Freedom that allows you to explore and / or do side quests
[*]The Story is well made and makes sense after a while
[*]There is a lot of stuff to do if you really want to do it
[*]The graphics are pretty good
[*]The cities feel alive
[*]The characters are well developed and have some depth
[*]Photomode – something I really love since I started to take screenshots more often
[/list]
[list][b]Cons[/b]
[*]The controls on the keyboard are a bit weird (which is nothing new but still an issue at times)
[*]The Photomode controls are not convenient for keyboard users
[*]Sometimes the FPS drops which is weird since my rig isnt the issue
[*]Some areas of the map seem too empty
[*]The voice of Bayek is too loud and there is no option to turn it down
[*]The game can be grindy at times
[/list]

So full disclosure- I never really got into the AC games. I've only played some of the first and second games and decided they weren't really for me. I've avoided every AC game since then. 

The main reason I bought this game was because I was itching for another an open-world game after finishing The Witcher 3, which blew me away. While the missions and story here dont have the same branching out like W3 does, this is still a fantastic game. 

Starting off with the protagonist- Bayek is awesome. He's strong, loyal, kind, agile and fierce. He's well written and the voice actor did an excellent job. If Ubi made another AC game with Bayek I'd probably buy it. Many of the supporting cast is fantastic as well. The main story is great and The Hidden Ones expansion tops it off perfectly in my opinion. The Curse of the Pharaohs was a lot of fun as well. I did them in that order.

I really like how much there is to explore and find in this game. I felt compelled to discover every fast travel location, completed every enemy camp and animal lair, found every treasure, completed all the side quests and of course all the main missions. I did everything. It was just fun to see what was out there in the world, get XP and level up to get better weapons and gear and make Bayek an ultimate badass and meet new and interesting NPCs. 

I love how if you find a weapon you really like you can take it to a blacksmith and upgrade it to your level to increase its damage. I must have carried the same weapon for at least 50 hours and i probably leveled it up a million times to max level 55. Thats a really cool option I think. 

And thankfully, at least for me- there isnt a "Vision" mode here like tons of other games, (where you hit a button and it shows/tags items, enemies, points of interest (poi) etc but the graphics go to shit). Instead in this game you hit a button and it puts little colored diamonds above loot, poi, etc without disrupting the graphics. And what I thought was an awesome addition was your eagle named Seru. He's always flying above you and you can instantly switch to him to hover around enemy camps to tag enemies, check terrain layouts, discover underground entrances, hidden treasures, and even harass enemies if you want! And the camera always zooms out to him and then zooms back to you without any fade outs or loading, very cool!

The only things I wish were different are the armor, level caps and horses. All weapons in the game have better/worse stats depending on what level they are of course, but armor is purely cosmetic. I get why Ubi did this so that people find a look they like and stick with it (or find something cooler), but I wish there were defense stats on them. And i wish you could do the same thing like with the weapons and upgrade them as you please. Being able to increase health, melee/ranged/tool damage but not defense seems a little baffling, but maybe its a balancing issue or something. Horses too dont have stats like at least how fast they can run, which was a little disappointing but not a huge deal. 

Moving on the level caps...the main game caps at level 40, and I hit that just exploring the world discovering locations and doing mostly everything except the main story. With The Hidden Ones expansion your level cap increases to 45, and the Pharaohs expansions tops it out at 55. Even if you max out you still earn Ability Points for every level though, which can be applied to anything in the skill tree, and if you have all those learned already you can add 1% extra damage for either melee, ranged, or tool damage to no end. I just wish there were a higher level cap than 55 with better weapons available. To put some of this in perspective- during my 90 hours with the game+expansions, I hit level 55 with an extra 31 ability points distributed to the previously mentioned melee/ranged/tool categories. I did not learn about 5 or 6 abilities though because i wasnt particularly interested in those. This game could easily increase the cap to 75 or even higher for nuts like me. And theres New Game+ as well which im not going to do but if its there i would think the level cap would go even higher but I understand there has to be a ceiling somewhere.

Overall though I loved just about every aspect of this game. Areas didnt feel crowded and there always seemed to be a way through instead of having to go all around or up a cliff just to get to where you need to go. Mission markers were clear, NPC's didnt get it the way and they dont die during escort missions either which is great. Theres just a ton of stuff the game does right and well. 

AC Odyssey is much the same although with a different protagonist (that ive read isnt nowhere near as great as Bayek though) and a somewhat bloated map, but I'll still check it out because you can Spartan kick enemies off ledges which seems comically fun at the very least. 

I bought the main game first on sale and held off on the expansions until I felt that I liked the game enough and wanted more of it. All in all, I think I paid like $4 more buying everything separately instead of getting the Gold edition from the start on sale. But overall I enjoyed just about every minute of it. Highly recommended!!!!

I've been constantly postponing playing the Assassin's Creed series for a long time.  I'm finally here to share my thoughts on AC: Origins, the first AC game I've finished.

Assassin's Creed: Origins is an open-world action role-playing video game, the 10th installment of the AC series. The story is set in Ancient Egypt during the Ptolemaic Period and deals with the origin of the assassin-templar conflict with the assassin faith. The game processes the story of Bayek, the first Assassin, a former Medjay who fought to protect his people from dangers.

-- In addition to what I said above, I can say that although I haven't played the series fully, I know that the AC series has always taken real events as its starting point. And this time, we witness the spread of Rome's Republic-Monarchy conflict to Ancient Egypt. Cleopatra was removed from the throne she claimed, and her brother Ptolemy ascended the throne. Cleopatra, who defended that Ptolemy was a puppet, also declared war for the pharaohship. At this point, Cleopatra will not hesitate to take advantage of even Rome's civil war. It is right in the middle of this turmoil that we are Bayek of Siwa chasing his own revenge story. --
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2815341124
While Bayek is normally expected to be a character who always frowns and sprints along the path of revenge due to his own story, he was created as a character who can find pleasure in the small details of life and has a sense of humor. That's why Bayek of Siwa took his place in the list of my favorite characters in my game life.

Let me tell you about the innovation in the AC series that comes with this game. Unlike previous games in the series, AC: Origins stands out for its role-playing innovation. The game has the must-have features of role-playing games such as a level system, ability system, and item system. It's just not that. There is also a crafting system. By collecting certain resources, you can improve your hidden blade, quiver, armor, and many other features. Also, if your level has increased and the weapon you like is no longer powerful, don't worry, because you can improve your weapon to the same level as you by going to a blacksmith. Here are all these and many other innovations that show us that AC: Origins has taken on the character of a role-playing game.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2820001476
Let me also tell you a little about the new combat system. Because I've never really enjoyed fighting so much before. :) In the new combat system, we can no longer counterattack with a single button and knock down the enemy with a single movement. Especially if our enemy is strong, we also need to actively use important movements such as dodging attacks and avoiding attacks. This also increases the enjoyment of the game.

Assassin's Creed Origins has a seriously huge map. The fact that the world is so vast offers us many places to explore. A new place we can explore may contain a new task, item, resource, or something new related to the story. In addition, the fact that small puzzles have been added to the game is also one of the great features. I have completed all the main missions, side missions, events, and question marks in the game in 100+ hours. I have enjoyed every hour of these 100+ hours. The graphics, in a word, look amazing. The specific mood of ancient Egypt is reflected very nicely. The in-game animations are also beautifully crafted. Although artificial intelligence is not perfect, it can perform much more logical movements than old games.(after a certain level of difficulty)

With all this told, I really liked AC: Origins. I had a satisfying gameplay experience with almost non-repetitive missions on such a huge map. I did my best and as much as I believed it was stupid to take revenge, I did my duty. Now I can say that [i]i'm fine with this, i'm not a father anymore, i'm not a husband, i'm not a Medjay. i'm a Hidden One[/i].

Summary:

In 2016, no Assassin's Creed games were announced or released as Ubisoft took a year off to polish their next AC game and boy have they delivered. Assassin's Creed Origins is a awesome comeback for the series and while it still has those core AC elements we know and love, the game has taken a different approach from it's predecessors. It now follows an RPG style game, where you level up and can customise your character with all sorts of loot. The minimap has been ditched in favour of The Witcher 3 compass style navigation and it makes exploring the world much more interesting and fun. Combat has also been revamped and no longer follows the old system of counter and kill.

Game world:

Ptolemaic Egypt is massive and each location is filled with mini objectives that you do to complete the area, for example killing the captain and/or looting all the treasure. Each district in Egypt offers hours of content and are all unique in apperance. Due to the absence of the minimap, locations are now marked with a ? icon and similar to The Witcher 3 they can be discovered upon while wandering the massive world. This is the biggest AC open world to date and it certainly delivers an authentic feeling of the time period the game is set in. There is so much side content in the world that you end up getting distracted and straying away from the main quest very easily. Each side quest is unique and offers different stories which means that it does not become repetitive quickly.

Narrative:

The game's narrative differs from the previous games as it is not about the fight between the Templars and Assassins. When you start the game in AC Origins, the Assassin order does not even exist. As you play through the game you will find out about the people and ideas that ultimatley lead to the Assassin order being created. Each main quest I played was interesting and it gave me little bits of information about the beggining of the Assassin order. We all have grown tired of the same old "Assassins vs Templars" and I think AC Origins story is a nice refreshment from all that stuff.

Combat:

Combat in Assassin's Creed Origins has been completley revamped. If you remember the old system of an enemy attacking you one at a time and you countering all their moves over and over, you can be glad that this is no longer how combat works. Because the game is RPG style the combat is signnificantly harder.  Enemies no longer attack one at a time but instead two or three would have a go at you at the same time. Before you could win fights just by countering when the symbol came up, however now to win combat scenarios you're going to have to be the same or a higher level than your enemis and also have strong weapons and gear equipped. This gives comabt in AC Origins variety as the enemies wouldn't wait one at a time. This combat change was greatly needed and I no longer rush in to a fort, due to it being harder than it was before.

Problems:

Assassin's Creed Origin's does not have much negatives however a major issue of this game is it's poor optimization. I have a GTX 970 4gb graphics card and I should be able to run the game at a solid 60 FPS due to me being able to run much more demanding games. I would always have around 45 FPS when playing but sometimes it would drop as low as 25 and it killed some of the enjoyment for me. Assassin's Creed on PC has generally had a bad history of optimization but I never really had it as bad as this. It stutters and lags at some intense moments but I'm glad I can at least mantain a playable FPS 90% of the time. The game eats up a lot of your CPU and Ram so if you have a less powerful CPU or less Ram you may encounter long loadings, stutter, textures not rendering quickly etc. These sort of ruin the experience and I wish Ubisoft would do better with AC on PC.

Conclusion:

You may ask "Should I get Assassin's Creed Origins?" the answer is yes. This game won't disappoint you it is filled with content and I am certain you will be spending hours trying to 100% this game. Assassin's Creed Origins has revived the series for many people and I believe that taking one year off has helped Ubisoft create an awesome AC game. If you're reluctant to give this game a go due to it's previous mistakes I would suggest you come back. This game deserves a chance it has in a way reinvented the series and I hope future releases can follow Origin's example.

After Assassin's Creed Unity, things looked grim for the AC franchise. After an embarrasing launch in an already turbulent year for Ubisoft, I became disinterested in the AC franchise after loyally following it since the first game. In some ways, this was to be expected after 3 games focusing solely on Ezio Auditore da Firenze, the franchise's most memorable character and the shift towards yearly releases.

Then I saw the trailer for Assassin's Creed Origins and my curiosity started. I pre-ordered the game literally the day before it came out. I dreaded the moment it became playable as I was fearing another Unity. And I am glad I was wrong. Assassin's Creed Origins is a true return to form for a franchise that has passed through a VERY rough phase.

The game is set during Ptolemic Egypt, a country with a history stretching back thousands of years. Once a proud kingdom, now a divided region, torn between Ptolemy XIII and his sister/wife Cleopatra fighting for control. At the same time, old tensions are flaring up again while a new emergent power is also taking an interest in Egypt. You play as Bayek of Siwa, a Medjay or a Protector.

The setting is very fascinating as it focuses on a period of civil war in a country that had a long history, a history that is visible all around the map in the game. The story is engaging, albeit at the start there are pacing issues but bear with them as it gets interesting later.

The gameplay is heavily influenced by Witcher 3 and I have to say, it works really well for this. The RPG element is useful and should be further improved in successive games. One element I agree is a tad problematic is the combat system. It takes a short time to learn but a long time to master.  The storyline is linear but this has always been the case with AC. What is open is how you tackle objectives or conduct assassinations, allowing you to take on enemies through a variety of ways.

However, for me one feature really stood out. On February 2018, Ubisoft released the Discovery Tour. It allows the player to explore the entire region without any limitations such as combat. To see the setting with complete freedom, to see the details the production crew put in is very impressive. The feature also has tours which focus on particular aspects of the era, from mummification rituals to Egyptian beer to Greek education to Roman crucifiction. As an archaeologist, I find it extremely well-researched and the production crew also explain certain design choices, like the Sphinx having colour even though by Cleopatra's time, it had long lost the colours. This way you appreciate the detail and effort they took to present that history and this could potentially be very useful in educating the public about the wonders of Ancient Egypt so it is a breath of fresh air in this day and age (*cough History Channel *cough).

All in all, I thoroughly recommend this game to everyone, old fans and new people interested in the franchise. You do not have to play the previous games in order to understand what is going on. The modern sections isn't that great but this franchise was always about the past. Full price is worth it but if you're strapped, wait for a sale. The wait would be worth it in the end. It seems that Ubisoft has learnt its lesson and is avoiding yearly releases. The franchise has the potential for a great comeback and can also serve in educating people who are interested in learning more about the setting (which in turn makes you appreciate the effort they took).

I’ve waited a long time for a good Assassin’s creed game. I loved the first game and second one was my favorite until now. Barely forced myself to finish AC3 and Unity was a complete crap. Didn’t even played Syndicate since I didn’t want to waste my time and money. But Origins surprised me.

Gameplay is similar to the previous games but improved. Combat is finally fixed and is quite fun, it’s not clunky and unresponsive anymore. It could be better of course, but I’m totally ok with how it is now, I love it. One thing which surprised me is archers. When you try kill them they run away and you end up chasing them, really nice. Climbing and running through obstacles is smooth as never before. You don’t get stuck anymore. Even when you’re riding your camel or horse you don’t get stuck behind object, you automatically jump over them. And small things like marking the objective on the map and then you simply press a button and you follow the road automatically until you reach your destination makes your life easier. Though I must say this doesn’t always work correctly, AI sometimes can’t find a correct path. Another small thing. Don’t you hate when you need to follow an npc and you both move at different pace when you run a little, then walk slowly? Now you move at the same pace as npc automatically, small but very good improvement. And you have a little friend – an eagle which is used to scout the area and mark the enemies and treasures. Also you can hunt animals for resources and you need resources to craft and improve your gear. Weapons and armor are done similarly to rpg games. Everything has levels now, you need to reach a certain level to equip a certain weapon or a piece of clothing. When you level up you get an ability point which is used to unlock new skills. Enemies are done in rpg manner too and the map is broken into zones by level, so like in rpg games you can't go to a 20lvl zone fight 20lvl enemies if you're only 5lvl.

Gameplay basically consists of doing the main quest and a bunch of side quests. Main quest has a decent story. Like that blockbuster movie which is fun to watch, you have a good time but it’s nothing too special. Most side quests are generic but some have really nice background stories and some are hilarious. But good side quests make maybe 5% off all quests.
I don’t want this game to be too complicated or difficult, you get a quest, you go to a marked location and do what is required. This is a relaxing game for me, you run around, kill people, uncover the map, climb structures, collect loot and so on. You can take a stealth approach or go Rambo style. And burning arrows, oh thank you for another small feature. When you take your bow and aim to the fire you get a flaming arrow. This is a nice little feature. Previous games felt a little boring and sometimes frustrating and annoying like Unity, in this one it doesn’t get boring while doing the same stuff over and over again. After each quest you want to do another one and then another one etc.

Graphics. Wow this game is gorgeous. I must say previous games were great looking too, but this is just another level. It’s stunning, architecture is beautifully done, it's almost photo realistic, the buildings are done to the smallest of detail. Also character models are of highest quality. No matter if your running around the city or inside some building, you're running through a field or ride your camel through a desert – everything looks stunning. And it has a photo mode. Press LS+RS to enter the photo mode. You get various filters and other adjustments. At first I thought you cannot take steam screenshots since the overlay didn’t disappear, but I found out if you wait a few seconds the overlay disappears and you can hit that F12. The detail is amazing, you can close up to animals, take portraits and see every little detail.

Now about the so much talked performance. I know some people are having problems but not me. This is one the most smoothest games I have. It runs very smooth at constant 60fps on ultra settings. No fps drops or anything, just locked 60fps, no difference Alexandria or desert. The game is really well optimized, I can’t say anything bad about performance.

Now on to negatives. Season pass price is too high. The full experience costs 90€ and if you buy it separately it’s 100€. That’s just too much. I'm not going to pay 40€ for a season pass when i don't even know if it's good or not.
Another negative is microtransactions. You can buy stuff for real money. I rather use cheats, but not going to spend a dime on mtx. No fucking way! While Ubisoft has improved a lot in the past years there’s still a room for improvement.
There's too little real content. The game is pretty short. The map is empty and filled with generic quests and question marks. There's nothing to do except clearing outposts and collecting worthless treasure. It lacks content.

If you’re a graphics whore like me or a fan of Assassin’s Creed it’s a good game to buy, actually the best game in the series after ACII. If you’re a fan of open world games and love some action it's a good choice. But it gets pretty boring after you finish the short story and lacks content. Get this on sale.

This was a difficult choice. "Do I recommend it?" and I've gone back and forth between "No, but" and "Yes, if" a lot. This is a stunning looking game, with some of the most amazing environments I've seen. You start in the town of Siwa, decently sized and lovingly detailed, and I thought it would be maybe 10% of the world map. No, it isn't even 1%. The lush Nile delta, the pyramids of Giza, Alexandria with its greek buildings, Memphis with its Egyptian. Mountains, deserts, valleys, villages, temples, monuments, garrisons, fields, breweries, butchers, brickmakers, weavers, slums, palaces. Everywhere you look you can see jawdropping vistas, and weeks and months and years of work put in by some of the best environmental artists in the business. Exploring this world and seeing the inhabitants go about their daily life is the best part of the game. The main plot on the other hand, is the usual drawn out cliched tales of revenge and supernatural conspiracies you would expect from the Assassin's Creed series, punctuated by AAA scenes of action bombast. Lovingly rendered, and very dumb. A bunch of people with nothing in common and no motivation apart from gaining power, being moustashe-twirlingly evil, and being members of the Order of Ancients  needs opposing, so around you go supposedly creating a better word by slitting their throats, and the throats of literally thousands of enemy soldiers just doing their job. 

The world is filled with quests, a few memorable, most of them forgettable MMO like fare - investigate this, explore that, kill him, find her. In order to finish the game you will have to do a fair few of these side quests, or you won't have a high enough level to stand a chance in later regions that open up. Combat is fairly satisfying, I played on hard and I died a fair number of times until I learned the different enemies and their strengths and weaknesses. When to block, when to dodge, when to shieldsmash and when to sneak around and assassinate.

Despite my complaints about the writing, the exploration and world is just so good that it, together with the non-violent Exploration Module which teach you about the history of Egypt is enough to tip this into a "Yes, you should absolutely get this." Just be aware that it will take a while to play through it, and don't try to force your way through as many MMO quests as possible. Do a few of the most interesting when you feel like it, and climb on top of a rookery or pyramid occasionally and take in the scenery.

At this point there are two main series of Assassin's Creed games...the first ones being the Altair/Ezio & Desmond games (Ac1, Ac2, Brotherhood, Revelations +Ac3) and then all the rest...

There's a definitive line drawn after Ac3 (even if that game wasn't good, it was still with Desmond and the original story... for better or worse!) The truth is after the ending of Assassin’s Creed itself in Ac 3 , Ubisoft departed greatly from the original gameplay and story (except one more game later that sadly didn't go out so well) and so, Assassin's Creed lost its identity to the point of not being recognizable even to the players of the first games, and yet at the same time, Ubisoft kept trying to exploit the success of the "name" and the original series by coming up with a new title (almost) every year because, who knows, maybe they were afraid of starting something new.

To be sincere and less subjective, there were some good attempts here...of course... 

The new series started with AC 4 Black Flag which was a good game, but... it didn't have ANYTHING to do with Assassin’s being a sea adventure... and pirates (?!)
Then Ac Unity arrived and it was finally, a return to what was like playing an Assasin's Creed game... it was about parkour, free movement, stealth, big city to climb, and other places to hide, but improved in some ways and the story side of things had potential. But the game had problems. 
The main story had the french revolution chronology completely messed up and disorganized, if you didn't knew about the history period it would be impossible to follow what was hapening in game, the side missions being copy paste of each other a hundred times, and incredibly, the voices of the French characters had english accent…
Then AC Syndicate was announced and after seeing some gameplay i decided just there... i wasn't even going to try that game. 

So after all this it's safe to say that i wasn't at all excited about Ac Origins. Of course i like Ancient Egypt as much as the next guy, but that doesn't mean Ubi can take any historical period they want,  just throw you in the middle of it with nice looking graphics and expect you to just like it already right ? I mean... that's what they did with the last three games but still :D

Ashraf Ismail was the director of Black Flag and again here in Ac Origins and it shows.
I didn't like Black Flag, just because i wasn't interested in playing a pirates game , but that wasn't a bad game.

With Ac Origins i do like the idea of being lost in the desert with a camel (or a Legendary horse! ;) and this comes from someone who played a lot of Egypt games back in the 90s , i liked them  but after so much Egypt i was pretty tired (especially because all the games were similar) but with Ac Origins, to say it goes deep into Egyptian mythology (without being too heavy, if you are just a casual) but deep enough that it does seem to add something more, to show Egypt like you never seen before, like they done a proper investigation and respected the subject (not unlike what they did with the French Revolution) that is saying a lot.

And while the main story of this game... fails to do justice, if you explore the map enough and go deep, very deep in its land, you will be surprised of how many things you can find.

To be honest here, this is possibly the least Assassin's Creed game of all Assassin's Creed... and that's good! when Assassin's Creed Origins forgets everything about Assassin's Creed and it just lets itself be what it is, a game about Ancien Egypt with great historical research a great land to explore and great gaming parts, it just shines and amazes and becomes one of the better games that came out of the Ubisoft factory since Patrice Désilets, the creator of Assassin’s Creed, left the company. 

Then at the end, same as Black Flag, when it tries to relate with the firsts games it is too little to late... the connection to those games comes just at the last moment of the last couple of missions, some special objects and symbols here and there over the game...some bad excuses for the origin of some traditions... it seems forced and unnecesary...

In fact, Ashraf Ismail's game could be even better if he just wasn't trying to continue with the impossible task of relaunching again and again the Assassin's Creed saga wich has long ended since 2012.

As for the game itself, Assassin's Creed Origins takes chances, it dares to be quite different from the previous Assassin's creed games, and that's one of the reasons it works so well (as a game) It is fun, it makes sense, it is full of great characters that are full of life and expression (it is indeed a beautiful game to take photographs!) and in the end it does show respect for the Assassin's Creed legacy, (although the main story fails, the game and the exploration works excellent, including the side activities.)

Contrary to previous games in these last years, the side missions are generally good and sometimes pretty good, there are also other sides activities like the circle of stones wich is a nice adition to relax, the gladiator arena and also you have many tombs to explore (and the pyramids of course) which is great although i would've prefered more in depth exploration with them) 

As for the main story it has a rough start,  there is a short 3 minutes video, and that's it, you don't totally get Bayek at first, who he is, what he wants, why he is doing what he's doing (you start already with one assasination done and you don't know why) and it takes a long time to even finish the prologue (the main titles comes up after playing several hours) But...once the story starts going, and you meet Aya the game finds its rythm and it flows really well (as an Ancient Egypt game where you are a Medjay) and it has nothing to do with anything else really.
Then towards the end, the brotherhood is created...but... it seems unrelated, there's no real origin story there’s, just the spark, but then nothing happens . You don't get to see how it connects to the future chapters of the series. 

Then the bad guys, the so called "The order" are unmasked but you never get to know anything about them really... and whats up with the head these guys worship? 

And even before the ending, the main story of this game while it is well represented, and well acted, it does come out as short and doesn't have a lot of development.
The main missions are 20. By comparison the side missions are more than 100!! and that without counting tombs, and other side activities. All that side content, in this game is pretty well done, but i would GLADLY change half of that content, for more main missions to develop more the main characters and the main story. In fact, the game is really too long and at the same time feels too short because of a very weak main campaign. For example, the main character Aya is pretty interesting at first, but finally you don't get to see her too much (aside from being badass wich is cool) ... but in the end she becomes a little shallow) By comparison for example, Elise from Ac Unity even in that mess of a story manages to develop a lot and i still think she's the better female protagonist of any Ac game (yeah, even better than Aveline in Ac Liberation). And it doesn't do any good to just have so much side content if the main story suffers. Because that's all that remains long after the end.

Now that I have 100% the game and have more than 100 hours in it I feel I can write a final review of the game. 

I will say now that if you are one of those people that thought Black Flag didn't really feel like an AC game then this game will probably also disappoint you. 

Whist its a huge improvement over the last few AC games, and probably the best AC game since Black Flag, it still has problems, and one of them is very big. I will try to keep it as spoiler free as possible, but there is one point I may ruin that happens very early on in the story that I would not consider a spoiler but some people may, so be warned. 
 
I will start with the good things. 
 
-The open world is amazing, huge and fun to explore and has tones of interesting things to do 
 
-The new side quest system is really good with over 100 unique side quests which makes the game feel more fleshed out, and the side content is actually fun for once instead of collecting chests and animus fragments from all over the map 
 
-Almost no collectibles 
 
-The new combat is really fun and much more challenging. Also makes stealth more meaningful 
 
-Interesting main character  
 
-Modern day is back, and whilst its still not as good as it used to its a huge step up over the last 4 games 
 
 
Now the two small issues I have are:
 
-Very few historical characters. There is only really 3 major ones.  
Cleopatra who is the main one, Caesar who is only in the end of the game, and Ptolemy who is only in 1 main cutscene. None of them are in the game enough and feel like wasted potential. 
 
-Stealth feels more clunky than the last 2 games. You almost never use cover for stealth and social stealth has been removed. The animations are pretty clunky which really ruins the flow. 
 
 
Now onto that major problem I mentioned. 
 
Well it saddens me to say, but the story in this game is shite. Seriously. I have never been this let down by a story in a video game in years, and AC games tend to have pretty good stories.  
 

For those who don't yet know, last year Ubisoft announced a new plan of how to approach stories in their video games, going away from narrative storys and focusing more on the world and letting the player make their own storys in the world. To quote them "less storytelling and more players experience." Sadly this new approach may be the death of the franchise, atleast to me and many old AC fans. 
 

The game starts of very messy with 3 different time periods, the main time period that you spend playing most of the game playing in, a flash back period 1 year before the main game where you find out about Bayek's Sons death (which is the main driving force for the story), and the modern day story. This jumping back and forth really confuses things and starts the game of badly. But it gets worse.  
 
Every single assassination target in the game is completely forgettable. I finished the story 2 days ago and cannot remember a single one of their names, and only about 2 of their faces. Since this is a game about killing people, having villains that are so forgettable and giving you no real reason to hate them, except that one of them killed your son (who was only on screen for 5 mins in a flashback) is a really bad idea for a story and gives you no motivation. 
 
The story telling also feels incredibly rushed, with most of your targets being assassinated in the very first mission they are introduced in, giving almost no character development and giving you no idea of what the are actually trying to achieve. The first assassination target is killed in the opening cut scene before you even start playing, the second target is killed in mission 2 and targets 3 and 4 are killed off screen so you don't even find out who they were.  

There is another instance late in the story where you are told by one of the side characters that two of the people you were working with have betrayed you, just out of the blue. This is meant to be a major twist in the story, so why the fuck did Ubisoft get some forgettable side character to just walk up and casually say "you have been betrayed". Non of the characters even seem to care, so why the fuck would the player care.
 
To make it even worse, there are pretty much no interesting side characters, so the main story ends up getting carried by Bayek and his wife Aya's relationship, which is the only part of the story which is actually interesting in any meaningful way. Most of the side quests felt like they had more depth and story to them than the main story.
 
I hate to say this, but unless Ubisoft change their mind on story telling in their games then the AC franchise is dead. I'm sure it will continue to sell well, but the main reason core fans like me play these games is for the amazing story and lore that this franchise has, and sadly this game completely failed in that regard, and if the next game has a story as bad is this one then I'm afraid alot of the main fans may lose faith in the franchise. 
 
I wish steam had a mixed rating since this is a really good game but the terrible story really lets the whole game down. I will give it a positive review for all the great improvements this game made, but if you are looking for a interesting narrative and emotional story go and buy one of the older AC games or the witcher 3 or something.
